page: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-1000s-amd is an instance in the Optimized Cloud Compute family, configured with 32 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory. The underlying CPU is an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, presenting 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set flags include AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, BMI2, and FMA, whereas AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. Local high-speed persistence is integrated via a 1000 GB NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without bundled hardware accelerators.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multicore throughput and memory bandwidth. The instance achieved 99,610.25 on stress-ng multi-core tests, placing it in the top 25%, alongside a top-tier single-core score of 3,132.38. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 346.3 GB/sec and write bandwidth hit 164.36 GB/sec, corroborated by a top-tier PassMark memory score of 3,040.25. In-memory data workloads demonstrated high concurrency capability, recording 76.91 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks. CPU-bound compilation under Clang scored 40,754.0 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 212.28 GB/sec.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio establishes high compute density while offering qualitative cost efficiency for CPU-intensive deployments that do not require massive per-core memory allocations. With 1000 GB of attached NVMe storage, this instance is suited for parallel software compilation, continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, in-memory caching tiers, and mid-sized model CPU inference.
description: Vultr voc-c-32c-64gb-1000s-amd is a compute-oriented instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute lineup, powered by a 32-vCPU AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz with 16 physical cores and dedicated thread allocation. It features 64.0 GB of system RAM, yielding a 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, combined with a 1000 GB local NVMe solid-state drive and one complimentary public IPv4 address. The CPU architecture supports AVX, AES-NI, and FMA instruction sets without AVX-512 extensions. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-quartile execution in multicore stress testing, Redis transactions at 76.91 million operations per second, large-block memory bandwidth, and Clang compilation tasks. Lacking a discrete GPU, it delivers dense, reliable parallel processing efficiency for build systems, distributed CI/CD pipelines, in-memory key-value caching, and CPU-based machine learning inference pipelines.
